title: When the mind is low
hookLine: chardi kala is not pretending; ask for help
tomorrow: the chemistry test comes back, and it's bad. now what?

lines: SITTING IN THE CAR, NOT GOING IN.
cards: Every text Simran has sent this week ends with a smiley. Bebe's doing great! Chem test Friday, all good!

Maya, who has known her since second grade, reads the smileys and sees something else. She walks over after school and finds Simran sitting in her car in the driveway, engine off, not going in. Simran says she's fine.
Then she says, chardi kala, right? Then she stops talking, and doesn't start again for a while.

teach.h: CHARDI KALA: FROM THE CLOSE OF ARDAS.
teach.b: Chardi kala comes from the close of Ardas. In paraphrase: Nanak, through the Name, may our spirits rise; by your will, may all be well. Sarbat da bhala, the good of all.
Notice the shape of it. It's a request.
Rising spirits are something Sikhs ask for, standing, at the close of Ardas.

teach.h: NOT A MASK, NOT A TEST.
teach.b: Not a mask you put on when you feel low, and not proof that you've failed if you can't find it. Chardi kala is not pretending.

Ardas itself is the Sikh way of asking for help out loud, and asking a person is the same move, turned sideways. Here's the line to tell a friend tonight: the Sikh phrase for high spirits sits inside a prayer of asking.
First Maya, there in the driveway: I'm not okay, I'm just tired of being the one who's okay. Then, that night, Harjit. And the next day, the school counselor, which is the hardest one.

None of them fix it in a day. But the smileys stop, and the real texts start. If low ever turns into thoughts of hurting yourself, call or text 988 in the US, or your local emergency number, right away.

how: Sikhs ask for chardi kala at the close of Ardas, and in hard times a family may ask the sangat to include someone in its Ardas, alongside talking to friends, elders, counselors or doctors.

games.q: what does “when the mind is low” mean?
o: keeping a smile on so nobody worries about you
asking for rising spirits, and for help, not faking them
praying alone until the low feeling passes

games.q: when the mind is low — tap the pairs.
p: rising spirits, asked for in Ardas
call or text if you might hurt yourself

s: chardi kala means always acting happy, whatever you feel
it's asked for in Ardas, not a mask; you can't fail it by being low.
the phrase chardi kala comes from the close of Ardas
Nanak, through the Name, may our spirits rise; by your will, may all be well.
asking a person for help shows weak faith
Ardas itself is asking for help out loud; asking a friend is the same move, turned sideways.

games.q: a cousin posts 'chardi kala!!' under every update, but hasn't left his room in days. what fits today?
o: message him privately: you don't have to be okay. want to talk?
post 'chardi kala!!' back, so he knows the family is upbeat too.
leave it; if he says chardi kala, his spirits must be fine.
games.why: chardi kala is asked for, not performed. a quiet, honest door is closer to Ardas than a cheerful mask.

practice: Make a small plan in your head. First, one person you could tell the truth to when your mind is low. Then the thing most likely to stop you, maybe not wanting to be a burden.
Then the plan: when that thought shows up, the first words you'll say to them.

wordCard.voice: When the mind is low. Chardi kala is asked for in Ardas, not faked, and asking a person for help is part of the same prayer.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: chardi kala, rising spirits, asked for at the close of Ardas.

carryVoice: Here's the line: ask for help, the way Ardas asks out loud. Day 1720, said out loud.
